title: Physical EFT Operator Contracts and Power Counting

items.title: Physical EFT operator data and power-counting contract
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; finite-jet contract, exact quotient representatives, supplier scale conventions, sources, and current dependency interfaces recorded; readiness ready.
items.statement:
Use four-dimensional Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, coordinates $x^0=ct$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and natural units $c=\hbar=1$ for mass-dimension counting. A **physical EFT operator contract** is a record of the following selected model data; none of the selections is inferred from an operator's name.

Here an EFT is an adopted low-energy model whose local Lagrangian is organized by specified fields, symmetries, coefficients, and a finite retained order; this definition implies no ultraviolet completion or physical realization. First choose a finite set $I$ of field species. For each $i\in I$, specify a finite-dimensional complex graded space $\Phi_i=\Phi_i^{\bar 0}\oplus\Phi_i^{\bar 1}$, its bosonic or fermionic parity, its smooth field domain on $M$, any reality condition, and its assigned rational engineering weight $\Delta_i$. Even fields are smooth maps $M\to\Phi_i^{\bar 0}$; odd field components take values in a fixed Grassmann algebra with smooth coefficient functions. A spurion is a fixed, non-dynamical parameter assigned a representation and engineering weight, used to record a declared symmetry-breaking insertion. The proper orthochronous Lorentz group is $SO^+(1,3)=\{L\in GL_4(\mathbb R):L^T\eta L=\eta,\ \det L=1,\ L^0{}_0\ge1\}$; specify its finite-dimensional action on all spacetime indices and require each Lagrangian density to be a Lorentz scalar. State the full gauge and flavor actions on every field, index, and spurion. A flavor symmetry that is absent is recorded as trivial; an approximate or explicitly broken symmetry requires its breaking spurions and weights to be listed.

For a non-Abelian gauge sector, specify the compact real gauge group with its actual global form, smooth right principal bundle, admitted bundle sectors, unitary representations, and a smooth principal connection. The connection is a Lie-algebra-valued one-form reproducing fundamental vertical vectors and transforming by the adjoint action; its local curvature is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, and the covariant derivative in a representation $\rho$ is $D_\mu\psi=\partial_\mu\psi+\rho_*(A_\mu)\psi$. The field and connection data must include their regularity and spacetime and internal index representations. These formulas use the right-principal-bundle convention fixed by the supplied gauge-geometry definitions.

The local operator algebra uses a separate finite-dimensional rational representation of a complex reductive affine algebraic group $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ on the finite jet generators. A contract must supply the maps and representations relating $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ to the selected compact gauge group and flavor group. It must either verify, on each retained finite jet space, that the algebraic invariant subspace is exactly the intended physical invariant space, or label the quotient as a formal algebraic selection only. Compactness of a real gauge group alone does not identify its invariant polynomials with those of an algebraic complexification.

Choose nonnegative integer cutoffs $r$ and $q$, a coefficient field (here $\mathbb C$) and its conjugation data, and a finite rational maximum engineering dimension $D_{\max}$. With derivatives assigned weight one, the local field-jet definition supplies the supercommutative polynomial module $P_r=\operatorname{Sym}(J_{r,\bar 0}^*)\otimes\Lambda(J_{r,\bar 1}^*)$ and its fixed-weight subspaces. For each weight $D$, let $W_D$ be the finite raw polynomial space, $V_D=W_D^{G_{\mathrm{alg}}}$ its invariant scalar subspace, and $\widetilde R_D$ the explicitly declared $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$-stable linear relation subspace. The selected operator quotient is $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/(\widetilde R_D\cap V_D)$: it identifies exactly the declared relations and makes no completeness claim about all EFT redundancies. For each retained $D$, choose a vector-space basis of $\mathcal Q_D$ and one representative $\mathcal O_\alpha\in V_D$ of each basis class; write $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{op}}$ for the resulting finite set of representative labels and $\Delta_\alpha$ for the weight of $\mathcal O_\alpha$. The finite jet, field-degree, and dimension cutoffs give a finite-dimensional retained space, and the fixed-cutoff monomial set gives finitely many retained weights and representatives.

For each $\widetilde R_D$, record each generator as a polynomial or Fierz identity, a total divergence under compact-support or stated boundary conditions, or a leading-equation or field-redefinition relation tied to an explicit base action and retained order. An equation-of-motion entry records its variational derivative and field multiplier; a field-redefinition entry records the local map, its inverse through the retained order, and all induced higher-order terms. The quotient is a definition of the declared relation space; its existence alone does not establish action, off-shell Green-function, quantum-measure, or scattering equivalence.

Choose the canonical-dimension power-counting scheme, coefficient truncation, and a nonnegative integer loop order $L_{\max}$. The formal loop label $\zeta$ is dimensionless bookkeeping and is not a convergence claim. The positive coefficient-suppression scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ is an adopted fixed model parameter, invariant under the declared Lorentz, gauge, and flavor actions, with mass dimension one (engineering weight one); this definition assigns it no numerical value or hierarchy. The retained local Lagrangian has the convention

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{\substack{\alpha\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{op}}\\\Delta_\alpha\le D_{\max}}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{L_{\max}}\zeta^\ell C_{\alpha,\ell}(\mu_W)\frac{\mathcal O_\alpha}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{\Delta_\alpha-4}},$$

where each $\mathcal O_\alpha$ has engineering weight $\Delta_\alpha$, each $C_{\alpha,\ell}$ is dimensionless in the stated natural units, and the chosen reality conditions make $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}$ real. This is canonical-dimension counting for the selected linear EFT; HEFT chiral counting and multi-scale SCET counting are different schemes and are not implied. A truncation order is not a numerical error bound, a coefficient prediction, or a derived renormalization-group flow.
Since $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ has engineering weight one, each retained summand has engineering weight four.

If the same application also uses a finite-regulator data record, retain its graph variables, measure, Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$, heavy mass $M$, external-energy bound $E$, and regulator cutoff $\Lambda$ with their supplied meanings. The operator-suppression scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, regulator cutoff $\Lambda$, $M$, $E$, and $\mu_W$ are distinct parameters unless an additional model input identifies them. A map from finite-graph variables to the continuum finite-jet operator data is also additional input; the finite-regulator definition supplies no such map or continuum limit.

items.physical_scope: A finite-jet, finite-order operator contract for a selected four-dimensional EFT, including its field representations, symmetry compatibility, coefficient convention, and canonical-dimension/loop truncation. It proves no complete SMEFT or HEFT classification, coefficient calculation, numerical truncation error, continuum limit, or empirical realization.
items.axiom_base: ZF + AC_omega, inherited through the declared non-Abelian gauge and principal-connection data; no full Axiom of Choice is asserted.

items.title: A finite-order SU(2) scalar operator contract
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; complete physical example, conditional proof, source limits, and current dependency interfaces recorded; readiness ready.
items.statement: Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the supplied gauge datum. Use $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $c=\hbar=1$. Let $SU(2)=\{u\in GL_2(\mathbb C):u^\dagger u=I,\det u=1\}$. Use the trivial right principal bundle $P=M\times SU(2)$ with projection $\pi(x,g)=x$ and right action $(x,g)h=(x,gh)$. Its product connection has horizontal spaces $\mathcal H_{(x,g)}=T_xM\times\{0_g\}\subset T_xM\times T_gSU(2)$, complementary to the vertical spaces $\{0_x\}\times T_gSU(2)$ and invariant under the right action. The associated $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued connection form $\omega$ has kernel $\mathcal H$; for the global section $s(x)=(x,e)$ its potential is $A=s^*\omega=0$, hence $A_\mu=0$. Gauge transformations are smooth maps $u:M\to SU(2)$ acting by $H(x)\mapsto u(x)H(x)$ and $\widetilde H(x)\mapsto\widetilde H(x)u(x)^{-1}$. Take one even Lorentz-scalar complex doublet $H\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb C^2)$ in the standard unitary representation. Before imposing the real-action condition, treat an independent dual field $\widetilde H\in C^\infty(M,(\mathbb C^2)^*)$ as a smooth field variable. In the complex-algebraic polynomial model, use $G_{\mathrm{alg}}=SO(\eta,\mathbb C)\times SL(2,\mathbb C)$, with $SO(\eta,\mathbb C)=\{L\in GL_4(\mathbb C):L^T\eta L=\eta,\det L=1\}$ and $SL(2,\mathbb C)=\{g\in GL_2(\mathbb C):\det g=1\}$. The orthogonal factor acts trivially on these Lorentz-scalar fields, and the special-linear factor acts by the standard and dual representations. Here $SO^+(1,3)=\{L\in GL_4(\mathbb R):L^T\eta L=\eta,\det L=1,L^0{}_0\ge1\}$, and the physical Lorentz and gauge groups map to $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ by $(L,u)\mapsto(L,u)$, viewing $L$ as a complex matrix and $u\in SU(2)$ as a matrix in $SL(2,\mathbb C)$; the standard and dual actions restrict to the specified physical actions. Impose $\widetilde H=H^\dagger$ for the real action. Take no flavor symmetry, field weight one, derivative cutoff $r=0$, maximum field degree $q=6$, retained engineering dimension $D_{\max}=6$, loop order $L_{\max}=0$, and a positive scalar coefficient scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ of mass dimension one as assigned by the physical EFT operator contract. For this illustration the declared relation subspace is zero. Then $\mathcal O_2=\widetilde H H$, $\mathcal O_4=(\widetilde H H)^2$, and $\mathcal O_6=(\widetilde H H)^3$ are gauge-invariant scalar polynomials of engineering dimensions $2$, $4$, and $6$. With real dimensionless $C_6$, the term $C_6\mathcal O_6/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2$ has Lagrangian density dimension $4$ and belongs to this dimension-six truncation. For $a,b\in\{1,2\}$, define $\varepsilon_{12}=1$, $\varepsilon_{21}=-1$, and $\varepsilon_{11}=\varepsilon_{22}=0$; then the antisymmetric polynomial $\varepsilon_{ab}H^aH^b$ vanishes because the even field components commute. This is a finite scalar-sector illustration, not a complete $SU(2)$ EFT basis or a claim that these coefficients describe nature.

items.title: Scalar derivative operator reduction at fixed EFT order
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; complete physical example, conditional proof, source limits, and current dependency interfaces recorded; readiness ready.
items.statement:
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the supplied gauge datum. Use $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, coordinates $x^0=ct$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $SU(2)=\{u\in GL_2(\mathbb C):u^\dagger u=I,\det u=1\}$ act on a fixed trivial right principal gauge bundle, and let $\phi\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ be an even real Lorentz-scalar of engineering weight one in the trivial $SU(2)$ representation. Let the global group $\mathbb Z_2=\{1,-1\}$ act by $\phi\mapsto-\phi$. The finite-jet module is the complexification of this real scalar field with conjugation fixing $\phi$.

For the finite-jet quotient use $G_{\mathrm{alg}}=SO(\eta,\mathbb C)\times SL(2,\mathbb C)\times\mu_2$, where $SO(\eta,\mathbb C)=\{L\in GL_4(\mathbb C):L^T\eta L=\eta,\det L=1\}$, $SL(2,\mathbb C)=\{g\in GL_2(\mathbb C):\det g=1\}$, and $\mu_2=\{z\in\mathbb C:z^2=1\}$. The Lorentz factor acts on derivative indices, $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ acts trivially on $\phi$, and $\mu_2$ acts by sign. Here $SO^+(1,3)=\{L\in GL_4(\mathbb R):L^T\eta L=\eta,\det L=1,L^0{}_0\ge1\}$. At the finite field-representation level, the physical group $SO^+(1,3)\times SU(2)\times\mathbb Z_2$ maps to $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ by $(L,u,\sigma)\mapsto(L,I_2,\sigma)$, where $L$ is included as the same real matrix in $SO(\eta,\mathbb C)$, the gauge factor maps trivially, and $\sigma=\pm1$ is included as the same element of $\mu_2$. Thus each scalar jet transforms by the Lorentz action on its derivative indices, trivially under $SU(2)$, and by sign under $\mathbb Z_2$.

Let $m\ge0$ be a fixed mass spurion of engineering weight one, let $C\in\mathbb R$ be a fixed dimensionless scalar parameter, and let $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ be a fixed coefficient-suppression scale of engineering weight one. Treat $m,C,\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ as constant Lorentz scalars and $SU(2)$ gauge singlets that transform trivially under the physical $\mathbb Z_2$ and under the full $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$-action. Define $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ and adopt the base action

$$S_0[\phi]=-\frac12\int_M\bigl(\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi+m^2\phi^2\bigr)\,d^4x$$

and add the dimension-six correction

$$S_6[\phi]=\frac{C}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}\int_M\phi^2\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi\,d^4x.$$

For compactly supported $h$, define the leading Euler derivative by $DS_0[\phi](h)=\int_Mh\mathcal E_0(\phi)\,d^4x$; the calculation below verifies $\mathcal E_0(\phi)=(\Box-m^2)\phi$. Take derivative cutoff $r=2$, maximum field degree $q=4$, retained engineering dimension $D_{\max}=6$, and loop order $L_{\max}=0$. Let the exact declared dimension-six relation subspace be the $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$-invariant span of $\partial_\mu(\phi^3\partial^\mu\phi)$ and $\phi^3\mathcal E_0(\phi)$. All fields and variations have compact support, so the displayed integrations by parts have no boundary term. Retain terms through formal order $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{-2}$, with $O(\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{-4})$ denoting terms at least quadratic in the formal bookkeeping parameter $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{-2}$, not a numerical error bound. Then $\phi^2\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi$ represents $-\frac{m^2}{3}\phi^4$ in this quotient, and the local field substitution $\phi_{\mathrm{old}}=\phi+\frac{C}{3\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}\phi^3$ changes $S_0+S_6$ to $S_0-\frac{Cm^2}{3\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}\int_M\phi^4\,d^4x+O(\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{-4})$. This is an action-level statement at the retained order only.
